title: Native GPU queue cannot resolve the Windows activity probe
body: Queued native GPU captures repeatedly emit `_gpu_powershell_path: command not found` from the live with-test-lock.sh, then report `comparison=INVALID-FOR-COMPARISON` and `windows-activity probe unavailable` while the Windows witness still runs. The queue optional native activity probe needs a resolvable PowerShell path or an explicit unavailable state that does not invalidate the GPU comparison.

title: Native run-root registration races on existing destination
body: A queued native editor build emitted `Move-Item : Cannot create a file when that file already exists` at Register-NativeRunRoot.ps1:31 while replacing the live root PID file. The build continued, but concurrent registrar writes should use a race-safe atomic replace or serialize the update so each wrapper can safely register its root.

title: AppFlow witness must flush the TCP request before waiting
body: The new native AppFlow witness wrote its JSON line with StreamWriter.WriteLine and immediately blocked on ReadLine without flushing. It returned an empty response even when the editor frame and channel were healthy. Flush the request (or enable AutoFlush) before waiting for the reply so the witness measures editor readiness rather than client buffering.

title: Keep report-only recipe GPU analysis out of synchronous registration
body: This VIXEN registration path synchronously queried row-walking metadata only to emit author warnings; the current GPU lowering service can block when a set consumer needs plan-service expansion. I gated the query behind explicit recipe tracing. Consolidate diagnostics behind a nonblocking analysis contract or a plan-aware service entry point so editor registration does not need a hand-written opt-in guard.
